Cairn Line.name: Cairn Line
Cairn Line.basicInfo:
A quiet row of small stone cairns across The Fade, each standing at the exact point where ground stops being ground — the Chamberlain's careful mapping of the region's end. Beyond the last cairn, color pales, sound gathers a half-step behind, and the hills give way to featureless mist. The cairns are identical: three stones each, unweathered, casting no shadow in the grey light. Walking the line is the only reliable way to hold a direction here.

Living Ecology: Transparent boundary flowers bloom between the three-stone markers, losing one color at each step toward the mist. Pearl moths use the line as a safe pollination route and make its drift visible before the stones are remeasured.
Cairn Line.hiddenInfo:
The cairns are not decoration — they are a measurement. Each one marks where the dimension's intention currently ends, and the line moves a little each season as the Fade thickens or thins. The Chamberlain rebuilds any that drift. Echo spirits avoid the line: something about the marked certainty of the stones repels them. One cairn, the seventh, is sometimes found with a fourth stone on it that matches no stone in the region; it vanishes again by morning.

Ecological Continuity: The occasional fourth stone is condensed soundless mineral deposited where two versions of a hill overlapped. It is a natural Fade phenomenon, not proof of unknown inhabitants.

The Dissolving Hills.name: The Dissolving Hills
The Dissolving Hills.basicInfo:
The fading upland of The Fade — gentle grey hills that lose color, sound, and certainty as they rise toward the region's edge. Grass here grows grey as frost, trees stand without leaves or with too many, and distances quietly stop agreeing with footsteps. It is not dangerous; it is unfinished. The hills are where the Demi-Plane simply stops deciding what it is.

Living Ecology: Translucent root-vines hold the reliable slopes together, and echo hares browse where grass still casts a shadow. Farther in, pearl moths appear as gaps in the mist until they turn back toward solid ground.
The Dissolving Hills.hiddenInfo:
The hills dissolve because the dimension never finished intending them — each walk through them takes a slightly different shape. Structures have appeared here overnight: a stair to nowhere, a doorway in a hillside, a lantern-lit path that leads back to its own start. Some are echoes of things the creator has seen or dreamed; none persist past a day or two. Mist pearls form where the fog of two different 'versions' of a hill slowly meet.

Ecological Continuity: Temporary stairs, doors, and paths are shapes produced by incomplete terrain or echoes of witnessed memory. They contain no fabricated residents and reveal no private history unless a concrete source placed that information there.

Dimensional Anchor Point.name: Dimensional Anchor Point
Dimensional Anchor Point.basicInfo:
The still center of The Last Edge — an unremarkable stretch of smooth grey ground that is, quietly, the single fixed coordinate from which the entire Demi-Plane is extrapolated. Nothing marks it: no pillar, no sigil, no glow. The light falls without direction, the air does not move, and standing on the exact point feels like standing in the pause between two thoughts. Anyone attuned to dimensional structure who stands here long enough will feel the whole dimension hanging from this one spot like a coat from a single nail.

Living Ecology: Sparse anchor lichen forms nine incomplete rings around the exact coordinate, while fixed-point beetles crawl closed paths that never cross. Once each cycle, a violet seam pulses outward through the otherwise shadowless stone.
Dimensional Anchor Point.hiddenInfo:
This is the most important place in the dimension and the least conspicuous. Destabilizing the anchor point would not collapse the Demi-Plane but set it drifting until it lost connection to the mortal world. The Mana Heart's guardian entity patrols here secretly whenever the creator is absent. Nullstone and fixed-point fragments are found only within a few hundred paces of the point — the ground's absolute stillness condenses them. The geometric formations occasionally found nearby are not buildings or ruins; they are the dimension's structure briefly becoming visible where stillness is deepest.

Ecological Continuity: The beetle paths, lichen color, and pulse timing provide redundant warning of drift. None creates a new portal, grants teleportation, or replaces the Demi-Plane Anchor item.

The Last Edge.name: The Last Edge
The Last Edge.basicInfo: The fixed southeastern rim of the Demi-Plane: smooth grey stone, directionless light, sparse white anchor lichen, and motionless air around the Dimensional Anchor Point. Nothing casts a shadow. Violet seams pulse once each cycle, fixed-point beetles trace closed routes, and rare grey needle-foxes drink condensation from the stone. The place remains austere and almost empty without being ecologically dead.
The Last Edge.hiddenInfo: Perfect rest protects the fixed coordinate, while anchor lichen, fixed-point beetles, and sentinel moths provide early warning of drift. Nullstone, grey crystal, and fixed-point fragments are collected only where the anchor naturally sheds them. Any anomalous object requires an actual origin—permitted traveler, defined intrusion, boundary shedding, or established development—and never appears solely to force a quest.
